skills.name: Aspect Ratio Helper
skills.description: Reduce a width×height to its simplest aspect ratio, name common ratios (16:9, 4:3, 1:1…), compute a missing dimension, and emit CSS aspect-ratio.

inputs.target: optional { width } or { height } to solve the other

skills.outputs: { ratio: 'w:h', decimal, name, css, solved }
skills.source: Original implementation; Euclid GCD reduction.

skills.name: Color Mix
skills.description: Mix two hex colors by a weight ratio, interpolating either raw sRGB channel values or gamma-correct linear-light values.

inputs.a: First hex color (#RGB or #RRGGBB). Returned when ratio = 0.
inputs.b: Second hex color (#RGB or #RRGGBB). Returned when ratio = 1.
inputs.ratio: Mix weight toward b, number in [0,1]. Optional, default 0.5.
inputs.space: Interpolation space: "srgb" (raw channels) or "linear" (gamma-decoded). Optional, default "srgb".

skills.outputs: { hex } — the mixed color as a lowercase "#rrggbb" string.
skills.source: Standard linear interpolation of color channels; sRGB transfer function per IEC 61966-2-1 (as used by CSS Color 4 color-mix()). Original implementation.

skills.name: Color Scheme Generator
skills.description: Generate a harmonic color scheme (complementary, triadic, tetradic, analogous, split-complementary) from a base hex color by rotating its hue in HSL space.

inputs.base: string — base color as hex, e.g. "#3366cc" or "36c" (leading # optional, 3 or 6 digits)
inputs.scheme: string (optional, default "complementary") — one of: complementary, triadic, tetradic, analogous, splitComplementary

skills.outputs: { base: string, scheme: string, colors: string[] } — colors as lowercase 6-digit hex, base first followed by rotated hues
skills.source: Standard color harmony wheel rotations and the CSS Color Module Level 3 HSL<->RGB conversion algorithm (W3C); implemented from the published formulas, no code copied.

skills.name: WCAG Contrast Checker
skills.description: Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio for a foreground/background hex pair and report AA/AAA pass/fail for normal and large text.
skills.outputs: { ratio, pass: { aaNormal, aaLarge, aaaNormal, aaaLarge } }
skills.source: Original implementation per WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance & contrast spec.

skills.name: Gradient Generator
skills.description: Interpolate N evenly-spaced stops between two hex colors (in HSL) and return the swatches plus a CSS linear-gradient string.
skills.outputs: { stops: hex[], css: string }
skills.source: Original implementation; HSL linear interpolation.

skills.name: Hex Color Normalize
skills.description: Normalize CSS hex colors: expand 3-digit shorthand (#abc -> #aabbcc), shorten 6-digit hex to shorthand when every channel is a doubled nibble (#aabbcc -> #abc), and lowercase. form 'long' always expands, 'short' requires a shortenable color (throws otherwise), 'auto' shortens when possible else expands.

inputs.hex: string - a 3- or 6-digit hex color, with or without leading '#' (e.g. '#AbC' or 'aabbcc')

skills.outputs: object { hex: string (normalized, lowercase, with leading '#'), canLong: boolean (always true for valid input), canShort: boolean (true when a 3-digit shorthand exists) }
skills.source: Original implementation for SkillForge; follows CSS Color hex notation rules.

skills.name: HSL Color Converter
skills.description: Convert colors between hex, RGB, and HSL representations. Accepts { hex } or { rgb: {r,g,b} } or { hsl: {h,s,l} } and returns all three forms.

inputs.hex: string — hex color like '#ff8000' or '#f80' (leading '#' optional)

skills.outputs: { hex: string ('#rrggbb'), rgb: { r, g, b } integers 0..255, hsl: { h, s, l } rounded to 1 decimal place }
skills.source: Standard HSL/RGB conversion formulas per CSS Color Module Level 3 (W3C) — original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Relative Luminance & Perceived Brightness
skills.description: Computes WCAG relative luminance (gamma-decoded 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B) and perceived brightness (sqrt(0.299r^2 + 0.587g^2 + 0.114b^2)/255 on gamma-encoded channels) for a hex color, plus an isDark flag (luminance < 0.5).

inputs.hex: string — hex color, 3 or 6 digits, with or without leading '#' (e.g. '#1a2b3c', 'fff')

skills.outputs: { luminance: number (0..1, WCAG relative luminance), perceivedBrightness: number (0..1), isDark: boolean }
skills.source: WCAG 2.1 relative luminance definition (W3C, sRGB linearization); perceived brightness per the HSP color model weights (0.299/0.587/0.114). Implemented from the published formulas.

skills.name: Nearest CSS Color
skills.description: Finds the nearest CSS named color to a given hex color using squared RGB distance over a built-in map of ~30 common CSS colors.

inputs.hex: string — a hex color like '#1a2b3c', '1a2b3c', '#abc', or 'abc' (case-insensitive)

skills.outputs: { name: string, hex: string, distance: number } — the nearest CSS named color, its canonical hex value, and the squared RGB distance
skills.source: Standard nearest-neighbor search using squared Euclidean distance in RGB space; color values from the CSS Color Module Level 4 named-colors table (W3C). Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: OKLCH Converter
skills.description: Convert between sRGB hex, OKLab, and OKLCH color spaces using Björn Ottosson's OKLab math. Accepts {hex} or {l,c,h}; returns hex plus OKLab and OKLCH coordinates.

inputs.hex: string — sRGB hex color like '#ff8800', '#f80', 'ff8800' (mutually exclusive with l/c/h)
inputs.l: number — OKLCH lightness in [0,1] (with c and h)
inputs.h: number — OKLCH hue in degrees (any finite number; normalized to [0,360))

skills.outputs: { hex: string ('#rrggbb', gamut-clamped), oklab: { L, a, b }, oklch: { l, c, h } }
skills.source: OKLab / OKLCH color space and matrices by Björn Ottosson, 'A perceptual color space for image processing' (bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab, public-domain reference math); sRGB transfer function per IEC 61966-2-1. Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Accessible Palette Generator
skills.description: Turn one base hex color into a harmonious 5-swatch palette with WCAG contrast ratings against black and white text.
skills.outputs: { swatches: [{ hex, hsl, contrastOnWhite, contrastOnBlack, readableOn }] }
skills.source: Original implementation; contrast math per WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance spec.

skills.name: OKLCH Palette Generator
skills.description: Generate a perceptually-even lightness ramp palette from a base hex color using the OKLCH color space. Converts sRGB -> OKLab -> OKLCH, varies lightness evenly at constant chroma and hue, then converts back to hex.

inputs.base: string (required) - base color as hex, e.g. '#3b82f6' or '3b82f6' or '#abc'
inputs.steps: integer (optional, default 5, 1..64) - number of swatches. With steps=1 the base color's own lightness is used.
inputs.lMin: number (optional, default 0.2) - lowest OKLCH lightness in the ramp (0..1)
inputs.lMax: number (optional, default 0.95) - highest OKLCH lightness in the ramp (0..1)

skills.outputs: { base: { hex, oklch: { l, c, h } }, swatches: [{ hex, oklch: { l, c, h } }] } - swatches ordered from lMin to lMax
skills.source: OKLab/OKLCH color space and sRGB<->OKLab conversion matrices by Bjorn Ottosson, 'A perceptual color space for image processing' (bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab, public domain / MIT). Implementation written from the published math, no code copied.

skills.name: Readable Text Color
skills.description: Given a background hex color, picks black or white text (whichever has the higher WCAG 2.x contrast ratio) and returns both contrast ratios, computed via sRGB relative luminance and (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05).

inputs.bg: Background color as a hex string: #RGB, #RRGGBB (leading '#' optional).

skills.outputs: { textColor: '#000000' | '#ffffff', contrastBlack: number, contrastWhite: number } — ratios rounded to 2 decimals.
skills.source: Original implementation of the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance and contrast-ratio formulas (W3C WCAG 2.1, sections on relative luminance and contrast ratio).

skills.name: Elevation Shadow Scale
skills.description: Generate a consistent elevation shadow scale (box-shadow tokens) from a base color and number of levels, emitting CSS custom properties.
skills.outputs: { shadows: [{ level, css }], css: string }
skills.source: Original implementation; layered-shadow elevation convention.

skills.name: Spacing Token Scale
skills.description: Generate a consistent spacing scale from a base unit and step ratio, returning px + rem tokens and a CSS variables block (--space-*).
skills.outputs: { tokens: [{ name, px, rem }], css: string }
skills.source: Original implementation; common 4px/8px spacing-scale conventions.

skills.name: Tailwind Shade Ramp Generator
skills.description: Generate a Tailwind-style shade ramp (50,100,...,900,950) from a base hex color by holding hue/saturation and scaling HSL lightness (50 ≈ 97% L, 500 = base, 950 ≈ 13% L).

inputs.hex: string — base color as hex, e.g. '#3b82f6', '3b82f6', or shorthand '#f00'

skills.outputs: { shades: { '50': hex, '100': hex, ..., '900': hex, '950': hex } } — 11 lowercase #rrggbb strings
skills.source: Standard RGB<->HSL conversion formulas (CSS Color Module Level 3, W3C; also Foley & van Dam, 'Computer Graphics: Principles and Practice'). Shade-scale convention modeled on Tailwind CSS's numeric palette naming. Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Tints & Shades
skills.description: Generate evenly spaced tints (mixed toward white) and shades (mixed toward black) of a base hex color. Returns base-first arrays; the mix fraction never reaches 1, though 8-bit rounding can land on pure white/black for bases within half a rounding step of an extreme (e.g. #fefefe).

inputs.base: string — hex color (#RGB, #RRGGBB, with or without leading #), required
inputs.steps: integer — number of swatches per ramp including the base (default 5, min 1, max 100)

skills.outputs: { base: string, steps: number, tints: string[], shades: string[] } — lowercase #rrggbb hex arrays, each starting with the base color
skills.source: Original implementation of standard tint/shade color mixing (linear RGB interpolation toward white/black).

skills.name: Modular Type Scale
skills.description: Build a modular typographic scale from a base size and ratio (e.g. 1.25 major third), returning px + rem for each step and a CSS variables block.
skills.outputs: { scale: [{ step, px, rem, name }], css: string }
skills.source: Original implementation of the classic modular-scale technique.

skills.name: WCAG Contrast Suggestion
skills.description: Given foreground and background hex colors, compute the WCAG contrast ratio and, if below the target (default 4.5:1 for AA normal text), suggest an adjusted foreground by stepping it toward black or white (whichever the background favors) until the target is met.

inputs.fg: string (required) - foreground color as hex, e.g. '#777777' or '#777'
inputs.bg: string (required) - background color as hex, e.g. '#ffffff' or '#fff'
inputs.target: number (optional, default 4.5) - contrast ratio to reach, must be in (1, 21]

skills.outputs: { original: string, suggested: string, ratio: number, passes: boolean } - original normalized fg hex, suggested fg hex, contrast ratio of suggested vs bg (rounded to 4 decimals), and whether it meets the target
skills.source: WCAG 2.1 relative luminance and contrast ratio definitions (W3C, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#dfn-relative-luminance and #dfn-contrast-ratio); original independent implementation, no code copied.

skills.name: Base64 Encode/Decode
skills.description: Encode or decode Base64 (standard alphabet with '=' padding) without Buffer or atob/btoa, safe for both browsers and Node. Treats strings as Latin-1 bytes (char codes 0-255).

inputs.encode: string (optional) — Latin-1 text to encode to Base64; char codes above 255 throw
inputs.decode: string (optional) — Base64 text to decode; must be valid standard Base64

skills.outputs: { result: string } — the encoded or decoded text
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard Base64 algorithm as specified in RFC 4648 section 4 (The Base 64 Alphabet).

skills.name: Case Convert
skills.description: Convert an identifier between camel, pascal, snake, kebab, and constant case by detecting word boundaries (camelCase transitions, underscores, hyphens, spaces).

inputs.text: string — the identifier to convert (any mix of cases/separators)

skills.outputs: { result: string, words: string[], to: string } — converted identifier, detected lowercase words, and the target case
skills.source: Standard identifier case-conversion conventions (camelCase/PascalCase/snake_case/kebab-case/CONSTANT_CASE) with regex word-boundary splitting; original implementation.

skills.name: CI Pipeline Generator
skills.description: Generate a CI workflow (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI) YAML from a project description: platform, language versions, install/test/lint commands.

inputs.node: string[] of versions, e.g. ['20','22'] (matrix); omit for the default

skills.outputs: { filename, yaml }
skills.source: GitHub Actions docs + actions/starter-workflows (MIT) as the canonical job shape; original implementation.

skills.name: Heuristic Code Review
skills.description: Scan a JS/TS snippet for common issues (debug logging, loose equality, TODOs, hardcoded secrets, empty catches) and return ranked findings with line numbers.
skills.outputs: { findings: [{ line, rule, severity, message }], score }
skills.source: Original rule set inspired by common ESLint/SonarQube heuristics.

skills.name: Conventional Commit Validator
skills.description: Validate and parse a Conventional Commits message (type(scope): subject) — checks allowed types, breaking-change markers, and subject rules.
skills.outputs: { valid, type, scope, breaking, subject, errors: string[] }
skills.source: Original implementation of the Conventional Commits 1.0.0 grammar.

skills.name: Cron Describe
skills.description: Translate a standard 5-field cron expression into a plain-English description, handling *, */n steps, a-b ranges, and a,b,c lists.

inputs.expr: string — a 5-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week

skills.outputs: { description: string, fields: { minute, hour, dayOfMonth, month, dayOfWeek } } — plain-English description plus the raw value of each cron field
skills.source: Original implementation following the POSIX/Vixie crontab(5) field syntax; phrasing conventions inspired by common cron-description tools (e.g. cronstrue), no code copied.

skills.name: Diff Summary
skills.description: Parse a unified diff string and report files changed, insertions, deletions, per-file stats, and a git-style one-line summary.

inputs.diff: string — unified diff text (as produced by `git diff` / `diff -u`)

skills.outputs: { filesChanged: number, insertions: number, deletions: number, files: [{ path: string, adds: number, dels: number }], summary: string }
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard unified diff format (POSIX diff -u / git diff) and git's diffstat --shortstat summary convention; no copied code.

skills.name: Dotenv Parse
skills.description: Parse .env file text into an object of key/value pairs. Handles KEY=VALUE lines, blank lines, # comments, surrounding quotes, and 'export KEY=VALUE' syntax. Lines without '=' are skipped. Prototype-ish keys (e.g. __proto__) are assigned safely as own properties.
skills.outputs: { env: object } — map of parsed environment variable names to string values.
skills.source: Original implementation for SkillForge, informed by the de-facto dotenv file format conventions (no code copied).

skills.name: Duration Parser & Formatter
skills.description: Parse duration strings like '1h30m', '90m', '2d4h', '45s' into total seconds, and format a number of seconds into a compact human-readable string like '1h 30m'.

inputs.parse: string (optional) — duration string composed of number+unit tokens using units d, h, m, s (e.g. '1h30m' or '1h 30m'; whitespace between tokens is allowed). Mutually exclusive with 'format'.
inputs.format: number (optional) — non-negative number of seconds to format. Mutually exclusive with 'parse'.

skills.outputs: { seconds: number } when parsing, or { text: string } when formatting.
skills.source: Standard unit-token duration parsing/formatting as popularized by Go's time.ParseDuration and the npm 'ms' convention; implemented independently from the unit-conversion definitions (1d=86400s, 1h=3600s, 1m=60s).

skills.name: Env Schema Validator
skills.description: Check a parsed env object against a schema of required/optional keys with type and pattern rules. Reports missing/invalid keys by name only — never echoes secret values.
skills.outputs: { valid, missing: string[], invalid: [{ key, reason }], checked }
skills.source: Original implementation; dotenv-schema style validation.

skills.name: Gitignore Generator
skills.description: Generate a combined .gitignore from an array of stack names using a small built-in template map (node, python, macos, jetbrains, vscode, rust).

inputs.stacks: string[] — stack names to include (case-insensitive), e.g. ['node', 'macos']

skills.outputs: { content: string (sectioned .gitignore text), unknown: string[] (unrecognized stack names) }
skills.source: Ignore patterns modeled on the community conventions popularized by github/gitignore (CC0) and gitignore.io; templates written from scratch, no copied code.

skills.name: JSON Diff
skills.description: Structural diff of two JSON values. Recursively walks both values and reports added, removed, and changed leaves/subtrees with dotted/bracketed paths like "a.b[0]".

inputs.a: any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) — the base value
inputs.b: any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) — the value to compare against a

skills.outputs: { added: [{path, value}], removed: [{path, value}], changed: [{path, from, to}], equal: boolean }
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard recursive tree-walk structural diff technique (as popularized by tools like deep-diff and JSON Patch generators); no code copied. Path notation follows JavaScript property-access syntax.

skills.name: JSON Path Getter
skills.description: Get the value at a dot/bracket path (e.g. "a.b[0].c") in a nested object/array. Returns { value, found } and never throws on missing paths; throws only on malformed or non-string paths. Prototype-polluting keys (__proto__, constructor, prototype) are treated as not found.

inputs.object: The root value (object/array/any) to look into.
inputs.path: String path using dot and bracket notation, e.g. "a.b[0].c", "[1].x", "a['weird key']". Empty string refers to the root.

skills.outputs: { value: any|null, found: boolean } — value is null when found is false.
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard dot/bracket property-path lookup convention popularized by lodash.get / JSONPath child-access syntax; no code copied.

skills.name: JSON Schema Inferrer
skills.description: Infer a minimal draft-07-style JSON Schema from an example JSON value: type detection (string/number/integer/boolean/null/array/object), object properties + required keys, and array items from the first element.

inputs.value: Example JSON value to infer a schema from (any JSON-serializable value: string, number, boolean, null, array, or plain object). Required.

skills.outputs: { schema: object } — a minimal draft-07-style JSON Schema describing the input value.
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard type-inference approach described by the JSON Schema draft-07 specification (json-schema.org, IETF draft handrews-json-schema-01). No code copied.

skills.name: Markdown TOC Generator
skills.description: Generates a table of contents from markdown ATX headings (# ... ######), allowing the CommonMark 0-3 leading spaces. Skips headings inside ``` or ~~~ fenced code blocks. Builds GitHub-style slug anchors (lowercase, spaces to hyphens, strip non-alphanumeric except hyphens) with -1/-2 suffixes for duplicates, guaranteed collision-free against previously emitted slugs. Respects maxDepth (default 3). Returns the TOC entries and a rendered markdown list indented by (level - 1) * 2 spaces.

inputs.markdown: string (required) — the markdown document to scan
inputs.maxDepth: integer 1-6 (optional, default 3) — include headings up to this level

skills.outputs: { toc: Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>, markdown: string } — toc entries in document order and a markdown bullet list of anchor links
skills.source: Original implementation; slug scheme modeled on the commonly documented GitHub heading-anchor convention.

skills.name: Query String Parser/Stringifier
skills.description: Parse URL query strings into objects (repeated keys become arrays) and stringify objects back into query strings, with URL encoding/decoding and leading '?' handling.

inputs.parse: string (optional) — a query string to parse, e.g. '?a=1&b=2&b=3'
inputs.stringify: object (optional) — a flat object to serialize; array values become repeated keys

skills.outputs: { query: object } when parsing, or { string: string } when stringifying
skills.source: Implements the standard application/x-www-form-urlencoded query-string convention (WHATWG URL spec); original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: SemVer Next-Version
skills.description: Determine the next semantic version from the current version plus commit types (feat/fix/breaking) or an explicit level. Handles pre-release resets.
skills.outputs: { current, next, bump }
skills.source: Original implementation per semver.org 2.0.0 + Conventional Commits mapping.

skills.name: Semver Compare
skills.description: Compare two semantic version strings x.y.z[-prerelease][+build] and return -1, 0, or 1. Precedence follows major, minor, patch, then prerelease identifiers (a version with a prerelease sorts before the same version without one). Build metadata is validated but ignored for precedence, per SemVer 2.0.0.

inputs.b: string — second semver to compare against a

skills.outputs: object { result: -1|0|1, aParsed: {major,minor,patch,prerelease,build}, bParsed: {major,minor,patch,prerelease,build} }
skills.source: Original implementation following the SemVer 2.0.0 precedence rules (semver.org).

skills.name: Slugify
skills.description: Convert a string into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII-fold common accented Latin characters, collapse non-alphanumeric runs into a separator, and trim.

options.maxLength: integer (optional) — maximum slug length; truncation never ends on a separator

skills.outputs: { slug: string }
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard slugification algorithm (lowercase + ASCII folding + non-alphanumeric collapsing), as popularized by Django's slugify and the npm 'slugify' package. No code copied.

skills.name: Test Scaffold Generator
skills.description: Parse a function signature (function/const arrow/method) and generate a node:test skeleton with a case per parameter plus edge-case stubs.

inputs.signature: a JS/TS function declaration or signature string

skills.outputs: { name, params: string[], test: string }
skills.source: Original implementation; simple signature parsing.

skills.name: UUID Inspect
skills.description: Validate a UUID string (8-4-4-4-12 hex layout) and report its version digit, variant family, and whether it is the nil UUID.
skills.outputs: { valid: boolean, version: number|null, variant: 'NCS'|'RFC4122'|'Microsoft'|'Future'|null, isNil: boolean }
skills.source: UUID layout, version field, and variant bit rules per RFC 4122 / RFC 9562 (ISO/IEC 9834-8). Original implementation; no code copied.

skills.name: Annualized Return
skills.description: Annualizes a total return over a number of periods using (1 + totalReturn)^(periodsPerYear / periods) - 1, rounded to 6 decimal places.

totalReturn.description: Total return over the whole span as a decimal (e.g. 0.1 for +10%). Must satisfy 1 + totalReturn > 0.

periods.description: Number of periods the total return spans. Must be > 0.

periodsPerYear.description: Periods per year (default 252 trading days). Must be > 0.

skills.outputs: { annualized: number } — the annualized return as a decimal, rounded to 6 decimal places.
skills.source: Standard annualization formula: (1 + R)^(N/n) - 1. Original implementation.

skills.name: Average True Range (ATR)
skills.description: Compute Wilder's Average True Range from OHLC bars — a volatility measure used for stops and position sizing.
skills.outputs: { atr: number[], latest, latestPct }
skills.source: Original implementation of Wilder's ATR (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978).

skills.name: Asset Beta vs Market
skills.description: Computes the beta of an asset relative to the market as sample covariance(asset, market) divided by sample variance(market), plus the Pearson correlation, over aligned return arrays.

inputs.asset: number[] - asset return series (length >= 2, aligned with market)
inputs.market: number[] - market return series (same length as asset)

skills.outputs: { beta: number, correlation: number } - beta = cov(asset,market)/var(market); correlation = cov/(std_asset*std_market), clamped to [-1, 1]; a constant asset series yields beta 0 and correlation 0 by convention
skills.source: Standard CAPM beta estimator (Sharpe, 1964) using sample covariance and variance (Bessel-corrected, n-1 denominator) and Pearson product-moment correlation. Implemented from the textbook formulas; no code copied.

skills.name: Bollinger Bands
skills.description: Compute Bollinger Bands (SMA ± k·stddev) over a close-price series and report the latest bar's %B and band width.
skills.outputs: { middle, upper, lower, latest: { percentB, bandwidth, signal } }
skills.source: Original implementation of Bollinger Bands (John Bollinger, 1980s).

skills.name: Compound Annual Growth Rate
skills.description: Computes the Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) and total return of an investment given its beginning value, ending value, and holding period in years. Results are rounded to 4 decimal places.

inputs.begin: number — beginning value of the investment (must be > 0)
inputs.end: number — ending value of the investment (must be >= 0)
inputs.years: number — holding period in years (must be > 0)

skills.outputs: { cagr: number, totalReturn: number } — both as decimal fractions rounded to 4dp (e.g. 0.0718 = 7.18%)
skills.source: Standard CAGR formula: (end/begin)^(1/years) - 1. Textbook finance definition (public domain mathematics); no code copied.

skills.name: Commodity Channel Index (CCI)
skills.description: Computes the Commodity Channel Index over OHLC bars: typical price = (high+low+close)/3; CCI = (typical - SMA(typical, period)) / (0.015 * mean absolute deviation of typical over period). Flat windows (zero mean deviation) yield 0.

inputs.bars: Array of bars: { high: number, low: number, close: number } (chronological order)

skills.outputs: { cci: number[], latest: number|null } — one CCI value per completed window (length bars.length - period + 1, empty if fewer bars than period); latest is the last value or null
skills.source: Standard Commodity Channel Index formula as introduced by Donald Lambert (Commodities magazine, 1980); implemented from the published definition, no code copied.

skills.name: Donchian Channels
skills.description: Computes Donchian Channels over a rolling window: upper band = highest high, lower band = lowest low, middle band = (upper + lower) / 2.

inputs.bars: Array of bar objects [{ high:number, low:number }], oldest first. Required.
inputs.period: Rolling window length (positive integer). Default 20. bars.length must be >= period.

skills.outputs: { upper:number[], lower:number[], middle:number[], latest:{ upper:number, lower:number, middle:number } } — arrays have length bars.length - period + 1, one entry per completed window.
skills.source: Original implementation of Richard Donchian's channel indicator (public-domain formula).

skills.name: Exponential Moving Average
skills.description: Computes the Exponential Moving Average of a price series. Uses smoothing factor k = 2/(period+1), seeded with the SMA of the first `period` prices.

inputs.prices: number[] — price series (finite numbers), length must be >= period

skills.outputs: { ema: number[], latest: number } — ema[0] is the SMA seed at index period-1; latest is the final EMA value
skills.source: Standard EMA formula as described in classical technical analysis literature (e.g. J. Welles Wilder / common TA references); original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Kelly Criterion
skills.description: Computes the Kelly criterion optimal bet fraction f* = p - (1-p)/b from win probability p and win/loss ratio b, clamped to 0 when negative, plus the half-Kelly fraction.

inputs.winLossRatio: number — average win divided by average loss (b), must be > 0

skills.outputs: { kelly: number, halfKelly: number } — optimal bet fraction (clamped at 0) and half of it
skills.source: Kelly criterion, J. L. Kelly Jr., 'A New Interpretation of Information Rate' (1956); standard formula f* = p - (1-p)/b. Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Keltner Channels
skills.description: Computes Keltner Channels: middle line = EMA(close, period); band width = mult * ATR(period), where ATR uses Wilder-smoothed true range. Returns aligned middle/upper/lower arrays and the latest values.

inputs.bars: Array of OHLC bars: [{ high:number, low:number, close:number }, ...]; length must be >= period + 1
inputs.period: Lookback period for EMA and ATR (positive integer, default 20)
inputs.mult: ATR multiplier for band width (finite number > 0, default 2)

skills.outputs: { middle:number[], upper:number[], lower:number[], atr:number[], latest:{ middle:number, upper:number, lower:number, atr:number } } — arrays aligned, element j corresponds to bars[period + j]
skills.source: Original implementation from the standard Keltner Channel definition (Chester Keltner, popularized by Linda Bradford Raschke): EMA midline with Wilder ATR bands.

skills.name: MACD Indicator
skills.description: Compute MACD line, signal line, and histogram (default 12/26/9 EMAs) over a close-price series, and flag the latest bullish/bearish crossover.
skills.outputs: { macd: number[], signal: number[], histogram: number[], latest, cross }
skills.source: Original implementation of Appel's MACD.

skills.name: Max Drawdown
skills.description: Computes the maximum drawdown of an equity/price series using a running-peak scan. Returns the worst (most negative) drawdown, the peak and trough indices/values, and the recovery index (first index after the trough where the series regains the peak), or null if never recovered.

inputs.series: number[] — equity or price values in chronological order; must be non-empty, finite, and strictly positive

skills.outputs: { maxDrawdown: number (<= 0, e.g. -0.25 for -25%), peakIndex: number, peakValue: number, troughIndex: number, troughValue: number, recoveryIndex: number|null, recovered: boolean }
skills.source: Standard running-peak maximum drawdown algorithm as commonly defined in quantitative finance literature (e.g. Magdon-Ismail & Atiya, 'Maximum Drawdown', Risk Magazine 2004). Original implementation; no code copied.

skills.name: Money Flow Index (MFI)
skills.description: Computes the Money Flow Index, a volume-weighted momentum oscillator. Typical price = (high+low+close)/3; raw money flow = typical*volume; over the period, positive and negative flows are summed and MFI = 100 - 100/(1 + positiveFlow/negativeFlow). Edge rules: zero negative flow with some positive flow -> 100; zero flow in both directions (flat prices or zero volume) -> 50 (neutral). Returns the MFI series, latest value, and an overbought/oversold/neutral signal.

inputs.bars: Array of OHLCV bars: [{ high:number, low:number, close:number, volume:number }, ...]. Must contain at least period+1 bars.

skills.outputs: { mfi: number[] (one value per bar starting at index `period`), latest: number, signal: 'overbought' | 'oversold' | 'neutral' }
skills.source: Standard Money Flow Index algorithm as introduced by Gene Quong and Avrum Soudack; implemented from the published formula (typical price money flow ratio), not from any copied code.

skills.name: Momentum Indicator
skills.description: Computes the momentum indicator over a price series: momentum[i] = price[i] - price[i-period]. Returns the momentum series, the latest value, and a simple up/down/flat signal.

prices.description: Price series in chronological order. Length must be greater than period.

skills.outputs: { momentum: number[] (length prices.length - period), latest: number, signal: 'up' | 'down' | 'flat' }
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard momentum indicator formula (price difference over a lookback period), a widely documented public-domain technical analysis concept.

skills.name: On-Balance Volume
skills.description: Computes the On-Balance Volume (OBV) series from price bars: cumulative volume added on up-closes, subtracted on down-closes, unchanged on equal closes.

inputs.bars: Array<{close:number, volume:number}> — chronological price bars (oldest first); at least one bar

skills.outputs: { obv: number[], latest: number, trend: 'rising'|'falling'|'flat' }
skills.source: Original implementation of the standard On-Balance Volume algorithm introduced by Joseph Granville, 'Granville's New Key to Stock Market Profits' (1963). No code copied.

skills.name: Pivot Points (Classic)
skills.description: Computes classic floor-trader pivot points (pivot plus three resistance and three support levels) from the prior period's high, low, and close.
skills.outputs: { pivot, r1, r2, r3, s1, s2, s3 } — classic pivot levels, each rounded to 4 decimal places
skills.source: Standard floor-trader (classic) pivot point formulas: P=(H+L+C)/3; R1=2P-L; S1=2P-H; R2=P+(H-L); S2=P-(H-L); R3=H+2(P-L); S3=L-2(H-P). Original implementation.

skills.name: Portfolio Risk/Return Metrics
skills.description: From a series of periodic returns, compute annualized return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, and max drawdown.
skills.outputs: { annualizedReturn, annualizedVol, sharpe, maxDrawdown }
skills.source: Original implementation; standard portfolio-statistics formulas.

skills.name: Risk-Based Position Sizing
skills.description: Compute share quantity and capital allocation so a stop-loss risks only a fixed percent of the account, respecting an optional max-position cap.
skills.outputs: { shares, riskPerShare, dollarRisk, positionValue, capped }
skills.source: Original implementation; standard fixed-fractional position sizing.

skills.name: Periodic Returns
skills.description: Convert a price series to periodic returns, either simple (arithmetic) returns price[i]/price[i-1] - 1 or log (continuously compounded) returns ln(price[i]/price[i-1]).

inputs.prices: number[] - price series, length >= 2, all values > 0

skills.outputs: { returns: number[], mode: "simple" | "log" } - returns has length prices.length - 1
skills.source: Standard financial return definitions: simple (arithmetic) and logarithmic (continuously compounded) returns, as described in standard quantitative finance texts (e.g. Tsay, Analysis of Financial Time Series). Original implementation.

skills.name: Rate of Change (ROC)
skills.description: Computes the Rate of Change momentum oscillator (percentage change over a lookback period) for a price series, with a rising/falling/flat signal from the latest value.

inputs.prices: number[] — price series in chronological order (length must be greater than period)

skills.outputs: { roc: number[], latest: number, signal: 'rising'|'falling'|'flat' } — ROC%, the last ROC value, and a sign-based momentum signal
skills.source: Standard Rate of Change (ROC) momentum indicator as described in classical technical analysis literature (e.g. Murphy, 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets'); implemented from the mathematical definition, no copied code.

skills.name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
skills.description: Compute Wilder's RSI over a close-price series and flag overbought (>70) / oversold (<30) conditions on the latest bar.
skills.outputs: { rsi: number[], latest, signal: 'overbought'|'oversold'|'neutral' }
skills.source: Original implementation of Wilder's RSI (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978).

skills.name: Rolling Annualized Sharpe Ratio
skills.description: Computes the rolling annualized Sharpe ratio over a sliding window from a series of periodic returns. Each window's Sharpe is mean(excess)/sampleStddev(excess)*sqrt(periodsPerYear), with excess = return - riskFree/periodsPerYear. Windows with zero standard deviation produce null.

inputs.returns: number[] - periodic returns (e.g. daily), length >= window
inputs.periodsPerYear: positive number - periods per year for annualization (default 252)

skills.outputs: { sharpe: (number|null)[], latest: number|null } - one entry per window (length = returns.length - window + 1); latest is the last entry
skills.source: Standard Sharpe ratio (W. F. Sharpe, 'Mutual Fund Performance', Journal of Business, 1966) with the conventional sqrt(periods-per-year) annualization; original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: SMA Crossover Backtest
skills.description: Backtest a fast/slow SMA crossover long-only strategy over a close-price series. Returns trades, total return, win rate, and max drawdown vs. buy-and-hold.
skills.outputs: { trades, strategyReturn, buyHoldReturn, winRate, maxDrawdown }
skills.source: Original implementation; standard SMA-crossover methodology.

skills.name: Sortino Ratio
skills.description: Computes the annualized Sortino ratio and downside deviation of a periodic returns series against a target (minimum acceptable) return.

inputs.returns: number[] - periodic returns as decimals (e.g. 0.01 = 1%), length >= 2
inputs.target: number (optional, default 0) - per-period target / minimum acceptable return
inputs.periodsPerYear: number (optional, default 252) - periods per year used for annualization

skills.outputs: { sortino: number|null, downsideDeviation: number } - sortino is null when the series has no downside deviation
skills.source: Standard Sortino ratio formulation (Sortino & Price, 1994): excess mean return over target divided by downside deviation, annualized by sqrt(periodsPerYear). Implemented from the published formula; no code copied.

skills.name: Stochastic Oscillator
skills.description: Computes the Stochastic Oscillator: %K over `period` bars (default 14) and %D as the SMA of %K over `dPeriod` (default 3). Returns latest values, full series, and an overbought (>80) / oversold (<20) signal.

inputs.bars: array of {high, low, close} numbers with low <= close <= high, ordered oldest -> newest; length >= period

skills.outputs: { period, dPeriod, k, d, kSeries, dSeries, signal } where k/d are the latest %K/%D (d is null if fewer than dPeriod %K values exist) and signal is 'overbought' | 'oversold' | 'neutral' based on the latest %K
skills.source: Standard Stochastic Oscillator formula by George C. Lane (1950s), as documented in public references (e.g. Wikipedia: Stochastic oscillator). Original implementation; no code copied.

skills.name: Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP)
skills.description: Computes the cumulative VWAP series from OHLCV bars using the typical price (high+low+close)/3, plus the latest value and the last close's position relative to it.

inputs.bars: Array of bars, each {high:number, low:number, close:number, volume:number}. At least one bar; volume >= 0; high >= low.

skills.outputs: { vwap: number[], latest: number, lastClose: number, position: 'above'|'below'|'equal' }
skills.source: Standard VWAP definition (cumulative sum of typical price times volume over cumulative volume), as described in public technical-analysis references (e.g. Wikipedia: Volume-weighted average price). Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Williams %R
skills.description: Computes the Williams %R momentum oscillator over OHLC bars with a rolling lookback period, returning the %R series, the latest value, and an overbought/oversold/neutral signal.

inputs.bars: Array of bar objects [{high, low, close}] in chronological order; finite numbers with low <= close <= high. Length must be >= period.

skills.outputs: { wr: number[] (%R per bar starting at index period-1, each in [-100, 0]), latest: number, signal: 'overbought' | 'oversold' | 'neutral' }
skills.source: Standard Williams %R formula as introduced by Larry Williams; reference definition per common technical-analysis literature (e.g. StockCharts / Wilder-era TA texts). Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Cosine Similarity
skills.description: Computes cosine similarity between two texts using term-frequency bag-of-words vectors over the union vocabulary. Tokenization: lowercase alphanumeric runs of length >= 2.
skills.outputs: { similarity: number } — cosine similarity in [0, 1]; both empty = 1, exactly one empty = 0
skills.source: Standard cosine similarity measure (Salton & McGill, Introduction to Modern Information Retrieval, 1983) applied to term-frequency vectors; original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Near-Duplicate Detector
skills.description: Cluster a list of texts by Jaccard similarity over word shingles, returning duplicate groups and a de-duplicated set of representatives.
skills.outputs: { groups: number[][], unique: number[], duplicates }
skills.source: Original implementation of shingled Jaccard near-duplicate clustering.

skills.name: Extractive Summary & Keywords
skills.description: Rank a document's sentences by term-frequency salience and return the top-N as a summary, plus the most significant keywords. Deterministic baseline for news/research pipelines.
skills.outputs: { summary: string[], keywords: [{ term, weight }] }
skills.source: Original implementation of classic TF-based extractive summarization.

skills.name: RSS / Atom Feed Parser
skills.description: Parse an RSS 2.0 or Atom feed XML string into a normalized { type, title, items:[{title,link,date,summary,id}] } shape. Pure parser core; fetching is a separate concern.
skills.outputs: { type: 'rss'|'atom', title, items: [{ title, link, date, summary, id }] }
skills.source: rss-parser / node-feedparser (MIT) behavior as reference; original zero-dep implementation.

skills.name: Word Frequency Distribution
skills.description: Computes a word frequency distribution over text: tokenizes into lowercase alphanumeric words, then returns total token count, unique word count, and the top-N most frequent words with counts and percentages.

top.description: Number of top entries to return (non-negative integer).

minLength.description: Minimum token length to count (positive integer).

skills.outputs: { total: number, unique: number, top: Array<{ word: string, count: number, pct: number }> } — top sorted by count descending (ties broken alphabetically), pct = count/total*100 rounded to 2 decimals.
skills.source: Standard bag-of-words frequency counting (term frequency), as described in classic information retrieval literature (e.g. Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, 'Introduction to Information Retrieval'). Original implementation; no code copied.

skills.name: Hashtag & Mention Extractor
skills.description: Extracts #hashtags, @mentions, and URLs from free text. Hashtags and mentions are returned lowercased and deduplicated in order of first appearance; URLs are returned as-is (deduplicated).

inputs.text: string — the text to scan for #hashtags, @mentions, and http(s) URLs

skills.outputs: { hashtags: string[], mentions: string[], urls: string[] } — hashtags/mentions lowercased+deduped (no leading #/@), urls as-is deduped
skills.source: Original implementation for SkillForge; regex-based tokenizer written from scratch.

skills.name: Jaccard Similarity
skills.description: Computes the Jaccard similarity coefficient between two texts over token sets (lowercased alphanumeric tokens of length >= 2). Returns similarity = |intersection| / |union|, plus the intersection and union sizes. Two empty token sets yield similarity 1.
skills.outputs: { similarity: number, intersection: number, union: number }
skills.source: Jaccard index (Paul Jaccard, 1901): standard set-similarity measure |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|. Original implementation of the well-known formula; no code copied.

skills.name: Keyword Density (SEO)
skills.description: Report unigram and bigram keyword density for a document and flag terms above an over-optimization threshold (SEO keyword stuffing).
skills.outputs: { totalWords, unigrams, bigrams, stuffing: [{ term, density }] }
skills.source: Original implementation of TF density with SEO stuffing heuristic.

skills.name: Levenshtein Edit Distance
skills.description: Computes the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings (counted in Unicode code points) and a normalized similarity score (1 - distance / max length).
skills.outputs: { distance: number, similarity: number } — edit distance and normalized similarity in [0, 1]
skills.source: Standard Levenshtein distance (V. Levenshtein, 1966) via the Wagner-Fischer dynamic programming algorithm with single-row optimization; original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Lorem Ipsum Generator
skills.description: Deterministic lorem-ipsum placeholder text generator. Cycles a fixed latin word list (no randomness) to produce a requested number of words, sentences, or paragraphs.

inputs.words: optional positive integer (max 100000) — number of words (single sentence). Default 20 when no key given.
inputs.sentences: optional positive integer (max 100000) — number of 8-word sentences.
inputs.paragraphs: optional positive integer (max 100000) — number of paragraphs (4 sentences of 8 words each), joined by blank lines.

skills.outputs: { text: string } — generated lorem-ipsum text.
skills.source: Original implementation; word list is the traditional public-domain 'Lorem ipsum' opening derived from Cicero's De finibus bonorum et malorum.

skills.name: Word N-grams
skills.description: Extract word n-grams from text and count their frequencies, returning the top n-grams sorted by count descending.

inputs.text: string — the input text to analyze (required)
inputs.top: integer >= 0 — max number of grams to return (default 10)

skills.outputs: { n, total, grams: [{ gram, count }] } — total is the number of n-gram occurrences; grams sorted by count desc, then gram asc
skills.source: Standard sliding-window word n-gram counting algorithm (classic NLP technique; see Jurafsky & Martin, 'Speech and Language Processing', ch. on n-gram language models). Original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Readability (Flesch / Flesch–Kincaid)
skills.description: Score text readability with Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid grade level, plus word/sentence/syllable counts.
skills.outputs: { readingEase, gradeLevel, words, sentences, syllables, interpretation }
skills.source: Original implementation of Flesch (1948) and Kincaid et al. (1975) formulas.

skills.name: Lexicon Sentiment Score
skills.description: Score text sentiment from a compact polarity lexicon with negation flipping, returning a normalized score, label, and the matched terms.
skills.outputs: { score, label, positives: string[], negatives: string[], tokens }
skills.source: Original implementation; compact hand-built polarity lexicon.

skills.name: English Stopword Filter
skills.description: Tokenizes text into lowercase alphanumeric tokens and removes common English stopwords, with optional user-supplied additional stopwords.
skills.outputs: { tokens: string[] (tokens kept after stopword removal, in order), removed: number, kept: number }
skills.source: Standard stopword-filtering preprocessing step from information retrieval (cf. Manning, Raghavan & Schütze, 'Introduction to Information Retrieval'); stopword list based on common English function words.

skills.name: TextRank Summary
skills.description: Extractive text summarization via TextRank: sentence similarity graph plus PageRank scoring, returning the top-N sentences in original document order.

inputs.sentences: integer >= 1 (optional, default 3) — number of sentences to include in the summary

skills.outputs: { summary: string[] (top-N sentences in original document order), scores: number[] (TextRank score per sentence of the full document, in document order) }
skills.source: TextRank algorithm as described in Mihalcea & Tarau, 'TextRank: Bringing Order into Text', EMNLP 2004. Original implementation; no code copied.

skills.name: TF-IDF
skills.description: Compute TF-IDF scores across a corpus of documents: per-doc scores for a given term, or the top-scoring terms of each document.

inputs.docs: string[] — the corpus; one string per document (required, non-empty)
inputs.term: string — optional term; if given, score this term in every doc
inputs.topK: number — optional, top terms per doc when no term is given (default 5)

skills.outputs: { N, scores } — N is the corpus size; with a term, scores is [{ doc, tf, tfidf }]; without, scores is per-doc arrays of [{ term, tfidf }]
skills.source: Standard TF-IDF weighting (Sparck Jones, 1972; Salton & Buckley, 1988) with smoothed idf = ln(N/(1+df))+1; original implementation, no copied code.

skills.name: Title Case
skills.description: Converts text to smart AP-style-ish title case: capitalizes the first and last words and all major words, lowercases a configurable set of minor words when they appear mid-title, and preserves existing ALL-CAPS acronyms.

inputs.text: string (required) — the text to convert to title case
inputs.minorWords: string[] (optional) — override list of minor words kept lowercase when not first or last; defaults to a/an/and/as/at/but/by/for/in/nor/of/on/or/per/the/to/vs/via

skills.outputs: { result: string } — the title-cased text
skills.source: Original implementation of the widely documented AP/Chicago-style headline-capitalization convention (capitalize first/last and major words, lowercase short conjunctions/articles/prepositions); no code copied.

skills.name: Tokenize
skills.description: Tokenize text into words and sentences: returns words (lowercased, matched by /[a-z0-9']+/gi and required to contain at least one letter or digit), sentences (split on [.!?]+, trimmed, non-empty), wordCount, sentenceCount, and uniqueWords.
skills.outputs: { words: string[], sentences: string[], wordCount: number, sentenceCount: number, uniqueWords: number }
skills.source: Standard regex-based word/sentence tokenization (word pattern /[a-z0-9']+/gi, sentence boundary [.!?]+), a common-knowledge NLP preprocessing technique. Original implementation; no copied code.

skills.name: Word Count & Text Statistics
skills.description: Computes text statistics: character counts (with and without spaces), words, sentences, paragraphs, average word length, average words per sentence, and estimated reading time in minutes (ceil(words/200)).

text.description: The text to analyze. Empty text yields all-zero statistics.

skills.outputs: Object { characters, charactersNoSpaces, words, sentences, paragraphs, avgWordLength, avgWordsPerSentence, estimatedReadingTimeMin }
skills.source: Standard text-statistics conventions: whitespace-delimited word tokenization, terminal-punctuation sentence segmentation ([.!?] followed by whitespace or end-of-text, so decimals/URLs do not split sentences), blank-line paragraph segmentation, and the common 200-words-per-minute reading-speed heuristic. Original implementation.
